# V1.7.3

Opened 2026-07-29, successor to [v1.7.2.md](v1.7.2.md).

**Why this doc exists:** v1.7.2 is a **single-item release batch** — W1 (the entitlement write-lock, `8854547`) is done and Alvin wants it cut to release immediately rather than held open behind a second, unrelated item. The cross-platform-contract freeze was booked into v1.7.2 as Item 2 earlier the same day and moved here so it couldn't hold that release.

**Scope narrowed 2026-08-03 — this is now a receipt-OCR-only release batch.** The web-app track was split into its own doc, [v1.7.4.md](v1.7.4.md), so the same reasoning that made v1.7.2 single-item applies here: receipt OCR can cut on its own the moment its de-risking corpus lands, without the web work holding it open. **Item 1 (freeze the cross-platform contract, Web Phase 0 W2) moved unchanged to [v1.7.4.md](v1.7.4.md) Item 1**, carrying its 2026-08-03 grill outcome with it. Book any further web/W-series work there.

**Numbering note:** the remaining items deliberately keep their original numbers (2, 3, 5) rather than shifting up, so existing cross-references — "gated on Item 5", "Item 2 Slice 1" — stay correct. The gaps are moves, not omissions: **Item 1** went to [v1.7.4.md](v1.7.4.md) with the web track, and **Item 4** (subcategories) went to [deferred.md](deferred.md) per that file's convention of keeping shelved work out of the active version doc.

**What's actually live here:** Item 2 (receipt scan) is the only non-deferred item, and it is gated on Item 5's spike, which is itself waiting on a real PH receipt corpus. Items 3 and 4 are shelved on business/hardware triggers.

## Item 2 — Receipt scan (photograph a receipt into a prefilled transaction)

- **Status:** **GRILLED + design-locked 2026-07-29 ([ADR-0062](../adr/0062-receipt-scan-ocr-prefilled-draft.md)) — not yet built.** ⚠️ **GATED on [Item 5](#item-5--receipt-scan-de-risking-spike-throwaway-runs-before-item-2-slice-1), which is itself ⏸️ DEFERRED 2026-08-03 — see Item 5 below.** Alvin has no receipt corpus on hand and gathering one will take days; rather than hold the rest of v1.7.3 open behind it, this item (and its gating spike) waits until he can supply photos — the design isn't in question, only the timing. **Not a separate decision from Item 5's deferral** — un-defer trigger is identical (see below). The design below stays locked — the follow-up grill does not reopen engine, gating, permission, entry points or the FAB rules. **Model: Opus, high effort** — a new dependency, a new capture path, a new permission, a parser, and a novel gesture control. **Three slices**, on-device verified between each (see Build order below). **No schema change, no Room change (stays v31), no Supabase migration**, and **no impact on the contract freeze ([v1.7.4.md Item 1](v1.7.4.md#item-1--freeze-the-cross-platform-contract-from-web-phase-0-w2))** — the parser is client-local, mints no deterministic ids, and writes only through existing synced columns.
- **Request:** photograph a receipt and have amount/merchant/date extracted into a prefilled transaction, so logging beats typing. Sourced from a 2026-07-29 competitive gap analysis against the Tarsi budget tracker.
- **Five codebase findings that reshaped the booking** (full detail in the ADR's Context):
  1. **The app has no camera capture at all** — receipts, notes and the couple banner are all *gallery pickers*, and no `CAMERA` permission is declared. "Scan" today means leaving the app entirely.
  2. **`ReceiptStrip` is dead last on the editor form** ([AddTransactionScreen.kt:391](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/presentation/AddTransactionScreen.kt#L391)) — which **kills the booking's "converge the two flows" option** as a primary entry: it's found only after the user has typed everything it would have filled.
  3. **The free receipt-photo cap is already 0** ([PlanLimits.kt:42](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/core/entitlement/PlanLimits.kt#L42), set by v1.6.7 Item 9) — so a premium differential exists without inventing one, which is what settled the gating question.
  4. **The prod APK is 5.1 MB**, making bundled-vs-downloaded OCR a real trade rather than a rounding error.
  5. **Receipts are stored at 1080 px / JPEG 85** — below reliable thermal-print legibility, so OCR must run *upstream* of the compression pipeline.
- **Change (locked — rationale and rejected alternatives in [ADR-0062](../adr/0062-receipt-scan-ocr-prefilled-draft.md), do not restate here):**
  - **Engine:** ML Kit Text Recognition v2, Latin, **bundled** (`com.google.mlkit:text-recognition`) — ~4 MB, 5.1 MB → ~9 MB, **measure at build**. Buys always-works-offline with no Play Services dependency and no "getting ready" state.
  - **Capture:** `TakePicture` + `FileProvider`, and **`CAMERA` is deliberately never declared** — `ACTION_IMAGE_CAPTURE` only requires it if declared. Camera **or gallery**, the latter covering GCash/Maya screenshots.
  - **Two entry points:** a scan CTA at the **top of the New transaction form**, plus a **scrollable FAB wheel** on Records (`＋` armed by default, `📷` peeking smaller; swipe to arm, small buttons directly tappable, **always resets to `＋`**, generic over an action list so voice slots in as a third). Coach mark per [ADR-0059](../adr/0059-coach-mark-coverage-is-discoverability-triage.md).
  - **Read** `Amount` / `Date` / merchant→`Note`, `Type` forced `EXPENSE`; **inferred** `Category` + `Account` from the user's **own transaction history** (no new schema, no merchant table, no LLM). **Only the inferred fields are captioned** — the read ones are verifiable against the photo shown at the top of the form.
  - **Not gated** — no new `Feature` entry. Premium keeps the photo, free has it read and dropped; structurally the [Export](v1.7.0.md#item-6--general-export-facility-csv--pdf--zip-receipt-photos-included) CSV-stays-free decision repeated.
  - **Photo goes two places:** in-app attachment (capped, premium-differentiated) and a **`Pictures/Love, Ipon`** gallery copy (free, never gated, **Settings → Finance toggle, default ON**). The gallery copy forces **the feature's only manifest change** — `WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` with `android:maxSdkVersion="28"`, runtime-requested on API 26–28 only.
  - **Failed read stays in the camera** — "Couldn't read that one" → Retake / Enter manually. A *partial* read is not a failure.
- **Build order (three slices, on-device verified between each):**
  1. **Scan → filled form** — dependency, capture (camera + gallery), OCR, parser, review with the photo shown, retake, attach via the existing cap path, gallery save + its Settings toggle. **This slice alone is the feature end-to-end.**
  2. **Learns from you** — history inference for `Category` + `Account`, with the "from your last SM Supermarket visit" captions.
  3. **The FAB wheel** — the Records door, generic over an action list, plus its coach mark.
- **Explicitly NOT in this item:** cropping or edge detection (retake is the fix), an LLM parser, a hardcoded PH merchant table, a premium gate on scanning, persisting the FAB's armed action, and the third (voice) wheel slot — which stays with [Item 3](#item-3--voice-command-natural-language-voice-input-to-log-a-transaction) until Horizon #3 un-defers it.
- **Verify:** build green; **tier-1 tests required** on the two pure pieces — the parser (total-line selection against `CASH`/`CHANGE`/`VATable` decoys, ambiguous `07/08/2026` month-first resolution plus the not-future/not-older-than-18-months bound, merchant cleaning) and the history matcher (normalisation incl. `#0142` branch codes, token-subset matching, most-frequent-then-most-recent tie-break, own-rows-only). Both are deterministic given fixed recognised text, so the OCR call itself needn't be mocked deep. On-device per slice, and **the "it got it wrong" edit path is mandatory, not just the golden path** — including a deliberately bad frame to exercise Retake, a first-scan-at-a-new-merchant (nothing inferred), and a second scan at the same merchant (inference now fires).

## Item 3 — Voice command (natural-language voice input to log a transaction)

- **Status:** ⏸️ **DEFERRED 2026-07-29, same day it was booked — returned to [Post-V1 Horizon #3 (AI companion)](project-build-progress.md), which already names "NL transaction entry" as one of its own sub-features.** Not shelved (Alvin actively wants it) and deliberately **not** moved to [deferred.md](deferred.md) — Horizon #3 is its single home, so it doesn't end up half-planned in two places. **Reason:** the research finding below killed the premise it was booked on. It was pulled out of Horizon #3 on the assumption it was independently buildable as a non-AI feature; on Android, for this app's market, it isn't. **Un-defer when** Horizon #3's hybrid funding model (capped app-funded free tier + BYOK) is designed and grilled — that decision, not this item, is the blocker. The stub is kept here rather than deleted because the hardware finding is the valuable output of the work, and it is what a future grill needs to start from. **Model when revived: Opus, high effort.**
- **Request:** log a transaction by voice using natural language (e.g. "Starbucks 250"), matching Tarsi's voice input. Sourced from the same 2026-07-29 competitive gap analysis.
- **Change (open, to be resolved at grill):**
  - **Disambiguate from Horizon #5, "Voice recording storage"** — audio-note recording/storage, ❌ dropped 2026-07-18 (Alvin: no longer wanted), and from CLAUDE.md's "Voice recording" out-of-scope line, which refers to that same dropped feature. This item is different: speech is transcribed to text and immediately discarded, nothing audio is ever stored. CLAUDE.md's out-of-scope list needs a clarifying amendment once this is grilled/locked (same pattern as the CSV/PDF export un-shelving), so a cold-start agent doesn't read "Voice recording" and assume this is blocked too.
  - STT engine: Android's built-in `SpeechRecognizer`/`RecognizerIntent` (free, zero new dependency) vs. a cloud STT service. Note the offline-first tension: on-device recognition exists (`EXTRA_PREFER_OFFLINE`, API 33+) but availability is device-dependent, and many devices route speech to Google's servers — so "voice works offline" is **not** a promise this can make on Android the way Tarsi makes it on iOS.
  - NL parsing: regex/heuristic extraction (amount + a merchant/category keyword match) vs. LLM-backed parsing. The latter pulls in Horizon #3's AI-companion cost/hybrid-model questions (capped free tier + BYOK) even for this "simple" feature, since Horizon #3 already names "NL transaction entry" as one of its own sub-features.
  - **⚠️ Research finding, 2026-07-29 — the Tarsi comparison does NOT port here, and this is the item's central problem.** Tarsi's voice input is genuinely LLM-backed ("offline AI chat… better understands natural expense and income entries"), running on **Apple Intelligence's on-device foundation model — free to the developer and present on every recent iPhone**. Android has no equivalent for this app's market: the counterpart, **Gemini Nano v3 via ML Kit GenAI, requires ~12GB+ RAM and a flagship chipset** (Snapdragon 8 Elite / 8 Gen 4, Tensor G5) plus AICore — as of mid-2026 roughly Pixel 10, Galaxy S26, OnePlus 15 and a few Oppo/Xiaomi flagships. **Alvin's own Transsion/MTK test device does not qualify, and neither does most of the budget-Android PH mass market this app targets** (see `rom-force-stop-nav-reset` memory for that device's constraints). So the three real options are: (a) heuristics/regex — free, universal, materially dumber than Tarsi's; (b) cloud LLM — per-call cost, breaks the offline-first stance, and cannot be decided independently of Horizon #3's funding model; (c) on-device LLM — free but functional for a small minority of users, i.e. a premium feature that silently doesn't work on the phones most buyers own. **Unlike Item 2, this item cannot be de-risked into a non-AI feature without accepting a visibly worse result than the app it's benchmarked against.** Grill should treat "build a deliberately simpler heuristic version" vs. "defer until Horizon #3 is funded/designed" as the live fork, not just an implementation detail.
  - Account/category resolution: "GCash 250" needs to resolve to a specific account and category from free text — decide whether ambiguous input prompts the user or best-guesses then leaves it editable.
  - Same premium-gating question as Item 2 — convenience layered on recording, not recording itself.
  - No ADR yet.
- **Verify:** build green; tier-1 tests for the NL-parsing usecase (pure Kotlin, given fixed transcribed text — same testability shape as Item 2's OCR parser). On-device check once built, covering at least one ambiguous/misheard input, not just the golden phrase.

## Item 5 — Receipt-scan de-risking spike (throwaway, runs BEFORE Item 2 Slice 1) ⏸️ DEFERRED 2026-08-03

- **Status:** ⏸️ **DEFERRED 2026-08-03 (Alvin)** — booked 2026-07-29, but he doesn't have a receipt corpus on hand right now and gathering one (10-15 real PH receipts, per the corpus spec below) will take days; rather than let that block progress on the rest of v1.7.3, this spike — and [Item 2](#item-2--receipt-scan-photograph-a-receipt-into-a-prefilled-transaction), which is gated on it — wait until he can supply photos. **Not shelved, no design change** — everything below is unchanged and ready to run the moment photos are available. **✅ Un-defer trigger:** Alvin has the corpus in hand (camera or gallery, doesn't need to be curated in advance — he can just hand over whatever he's collected). **Model: Sonnet, low effort** — throwaway instrumentation that makes no design decisions and ships no production code; the judgment happens *after*, when the output is read. **No schema change, no Room change (stays v31), no Supabase migration.** **Needs no grill of its own** — a spike is measurement, not design. Its output is the *input* to a second, narrow grill of [Item 2](#item-2--receipt-scan-photograph-a-receipt-into-a-prefilled-transaction) (see below). **Sequencing: this runs before Item 2 Slice 1, and its result can cancel Item 2.**
- **Request:** Alvin, 2026-07-29 — after [Item 2](#item-2--receipt-scan-photograph-a-receipt-into-a-prefilled-transaction) was grilled and design-locked into [ADR-0062](../adr/0062-receipt-scan-ocr-prefilled-draft.md), he wasn't satisfied with the grill and felt "there are some obvious things we are missing," and asked whether a re-grill or a higher-fidelity strategy (prototyping) would build more confidence. **The diagnosis, which is this item's reason for existing:** the first grill reasoned over the *codebase* and was strong there — it found the dead-last `ReceiptStrip`, the already-zero free cap, the 5.1 MB APK, the 1080px/JPEG-85 compression conflict. But it had **no receipt corpus and no running code**, so it specified a parser against imagined receipts and a capture flow against an imagined lifecycle. A second grill of the same shape cannot fix that; only real input can. Re-grilling was therefore **declined in favour of measuring first**.
- **The one question this answers:** **does bundled ML Kit Text Recognition v2 read real Philippine thermal receipts well enough for the feature to exist?** Faded, curled, narrow, dot-matrix, non-standard fonts. Nobody has measured it, and the entire three-slice plan in [ADR-0062](../adr/0062-receipt-scan-ocr-prefilled-draft.md) rests on it. ADR-0062 finding 5 already established that receipts are stored *below* reliable thermal-print legibility (1080 px / JPEG 85, [CompressReceiptUseCase](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/domain/usecase/CompressReceiptUseCase.kt)) — this measures the tier above that, the raw full-res frame.
- **Change (deliberately minimal — this is scaffolding, not a slice):**
  - **Throwaway branch, never committed, and explicitly NOT Item 2 Slice 1.** No use case, no ViewModel, no parser, no entry point, no nav change.
  - Add `com.google.mlkit:text-recognition` (Latin, bundled) to `gradle/libs.versions.toml` + [app/build.gradle.kts](../../app/build.gradle.kts) — **currently absent, confirmed**.
  - One throwaway screen: pick an image → run recognition → **dump the RAW recognised text** to the screen (and `Log.i`, not `Log.d`, per the `device-logd-suppressed` memory if run on Alvin's real device).
  - **Alvin supplies the receipt photos.** That is the whole value of the exercise — a synthetic or web-sourced receipt set would reproduce exactly the imagined-corpus flaw this spike exists to correct.
- **The corpus (deliberately mixed, 10–15 receipts):** SM / Puregold (long, clean, machine-printed), 7-Eleven, **Mercury Drug (for the SC/PWD discount lines)**, Jollibee, a **sari-sari scrap** (likely no total keyword at all), one **faded**, one **curled**, plus a **GCash/Maya screenshot as the easy control** — if the control fails, the harness is wrong, not the engine.
- **Three outputs, all for free from the same run:**
  1. **Recognition quality on real PH print** — the go/no-go.
  2. **A real corpus to write the parser against**, replacing the mental model. This is what makes the follow-up grill able to converge.
  3. **The actual measured APK delta.** ADR-0062 estimates ~4 MB (5.1 → ~9 MB) and explicitly says **"measure at build, not assumed"**; its own Consequences say if it lands materially above ~9 MB, decision 1 is what to revisit. This measures it before any production code is written.
- **⛔ Exit criteria — this spike is allowed to kill Item 2.** If recognition is poor on real PH thermal print, **the fix is not a better parser — it is revisiting whether to build [Item 2](#item-2--receipt-scan-photograph-a-receipt-into-a-prefilled-transaction) at all.** Booking that outcome up front is the point; a spike that can only ever say "proceed" isn't a spike.
- **Feeds a SECOND, NARROW grill of Item 2** — not a re-run of the settled design questions (engine, gating, permission, entry points, FAB rules all stay locked), but aimed squarely at the lifecycle and edge cases the first grill structurally could not reach. **Seeded with nine already-named gaps**, recorded here so they can't be lost:
  1. **When is the `Pictures/Love, Ipon` gallery copy written?** ADR-0062 decision 7 sends the photo there, but the draft is *unsaved* until Save — if the copy happens at capture, backing out pollutes the user's gallery with abandoned scans. Unanswered.
  2. **Who owns the new full-res pre-compression temp file** from `TakePicture` + `FileProvider`? Nothing in ADR-0062 owns its cleanup — and this **re-introduces the exact bug class [v1.7.0 Item 14](v1.7.0.md#item-14--orphaned-receipt-files-are-never-cleaned-up-device-storage-leak) (`161acec`, [CleanupOrphanedReceiptsUseCase](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/feature/transactions/domain/usecase/CleanupOrphanedReceiptsUseCase.kt)) already paid to fix.**
  3. **Parser fallback when a receipt has no total keyword at all** (sari-sari, small vendors). The grill designed against `CASH`/`CHANGE`/`VATable` decoys but assumed a `TOTAL` line exists.
  4. **SC/PWD discount and service-charge lines**, ubiquitous in PH, where "total" and "what I actually paid" diverge — and ADR-0062 doesn't say which one wins.
  5. **Long receipts whose total sits below the frame.** Retake is the stated fix, but only if the capture guidance tells the user what to frame.
  6. **EXIF rotation** — a rotated frame silently reads as garbage.
  7. **The free-user beat:** decision 4 shows the photo at the top of the form for verification, then `maxReceiptPhotos = 0` ([PlanLimits.kt](../../app/src/main/java/com/iponlove/app/core/entitlement/PlanLimits.kt)) silently drops it. No copy is designed for that moment.
  8. **No dedup** — scanning the same receipt twice produces two identical transactions, with no warning.
  9. **One receipt = one transaction / no line-item split.** Probably deliberate, but it's absent from ADR-0062's "Explicitly NOT" list, so it reads as overlooked rather than decided.
- **Explicitly NOT in this item:** any production code, any Item 2 slice, the parser itself, the history matcher, the FAB wheel, the `WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` manifest change, and committing the branch. **The FAB wheel was considered for a feel-prototype and deliberately left alone** — it's Slice 3, it always resets to `＋`, and its small buttons are directly tappable, so it cannot break the feature; its risk is aesthetic, not structural.
- **Verify:** the spike builds and runs, and produces readable raw text per receipt. **No tier-1 tests** — there is no pure logic here to test, and writing tests against throwaway scaffolding is waste. The real deliverable is a **written read on whether ADR-0062's parser design survives contact with the corpus**, plus the measured APK number, both recorded back into this item before Slice 1 is opened.
